# === VERDICT: BOTH mechanisms contribute (polar-map somewhat larger); loss-cubic real but NOT purely cubic ===

# 1. BOTH: map_frac ~0.77-0.80 (Muon polar-map nonlinearity) AND residual_frac ~0.66-0.69 (loss-cubic feedback) are large at every state (not orthogonal -> don't sum to 1). Neither exclusively explains the curvature change; the polar map is the larger single contributor.

# 2. NOT pure cubic: the e_loss scale ratio (0.5/1) is ~0.30-0.36 across all states, above the cubic ideal 0.25 -> consistent HIGHER-ORDER contamination at finite scale. Per the request, the loss-cubic residual must NOT be labeled a pure third-derivative force; it contains higher-order interactions.

# 3. Memory weakly modulates the cubic feedback: e_loss_norm and residual_frac rise slightly with longer memory (a2 > a1 >= a05; ~5-10% in e_loss_norm, resid_frac 0.66->0.69) -> real but small, within the higher-order-contamination uncertainty.

The both-mechanisms attribution is the resolved qualitative answer; a clean pure-cubic isolation is NOT established.
